primitives.name: Truncated Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter
primitives.verbatim_quote: **`EQ-GCP-001` — Truncated Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter (`python-docs-samples` / `rclone`):** $$\Delta t_k = \text{Uniform}\!\left(0,\; \min\!\left(T_{\max},\; T_0 \cdot 2^k\right)\right)$$ Eliminates synchronized retry storms across parallel agents hitting Google Drive, Docs, or GitHub APIs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$\\Delta t_k$:': 'Backoff delay at retry attempt k (seconds)', '$T_0$:': 'Initial base backoff (seconds, typically 0.5 or 1)', '$T_{\\max}$:': 'Maximum cap on backoff (seconds, typically 60)', '$k$:': 'Retry attempt number (integer, starting from 0)', '$\\text{Uniform}(a,b)$:': 'Continuous uniform distribution between a and b'}
primitives.assumptions: ['API request latency follows heavy-tailed distributions', 'Failure events are temporally clustered', 'Agents operate in parallel with shared network egress', 'HTTP 429/5xx errors indicate temporary resource contention']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple agents use identical deterministic backoff schedules, their retry bursts synchronize, causing cascading failures. Full jitter decorrelates these bursts, preventing saturation.

primitives.name: Content-Addressed Three-Way Bisync Invariant
primitives.verbatim_quote: **`EQ-GCP-002` — Content-Addressed Three-Way Bisync Invariant (`rclone`):** Given prior sync state $S_{t-1}$ and current endpoints $(A_t, B_t)$ with SHA-256 digests $(h(A_t), h(B_t))$: - If $h(A_t) = h(B_t)$: no-op (`0` bytes transferred).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$S_{t-1}$:': 'Prior synchronization state (content-addressed digest)', '$(A_t, B_t)$:': 'Current endpoint states (source, destination)', '$h(X)$:': 'SHA-256 content hash of state X (binary blob)', '$\\triangleq$ (defined as):': 'Equivalence relation for identical content'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Both endpoints support efficient content-digest computation', 'Storage backend guarantees immutable object keys', 'Network bandwidth is abundant relative to compute', 'Conflict resolution semantics are explicitly defined']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Without this invariant, naive timestamp-based syncing can lead to bidirectional overwrite loops or excessive data transfer when files change independently.

primitives.name: Resumable Multipart Chunk Size Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: **`EQ-GCP-003` — Resumable Multipart Chunk Size Optimization (`rclone` / `drive.googleapis.com`):** $$C^* = 2^{\lfloor \log_2(\sqrt{B \cdot \text{RTT} \cdot R_{\text{loss}}^{-1}}) \rfloor} \in [8\text{ MiB},\; 128\text{ MiB}]$$ Maximizes goodput over Google Drive `uploadType=resumable` while bounding retransmission cost on transient drops.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$C^*$:': 'Optimal multipart chunk size (bytes)', '$B$:': 'Available upload bandwidth (bits per second)', '$\\text{RTT}$:': 'Round-trip network latency (seconds)', '$R_{\\text{loss}}$:': 'Effective packet loss rate (dimensionless, e.g., 0.01 for 1%)', '$\\lfloor x \\rfloor$:': 'Floor function, rounding down to integer', 'MiB (mebibytes):': 'Binary megabyte = 2^20 bytes'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Network congestion follows a Markovian loss process', 'Server-side throughput scales linearly with chunk count', 'Transport layer supports efficient retransmission of failed chunks', 'Object storage has minimal per-object metadata overhead']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Choosing too small a chunk size leads to excessive control-plane overhead; too large increases recovery time after losses. This formula balances these tradeoffs under typical web-scale network conditions.

primitives.name: Bi-Temporal Point-in-Time (PIT) As-Of Join Invariant
primitives.verbatim_quote: **`EQ-GCP-006` — Bi-Temporal Point-in-Time (PIT) As-Of Join Invariant (`training-data-analyst`):** $$F(e, t_{\text{cut}}) = \arg\max_{(v, t_{\text{valid}}, t_{\text{tx}}) \in \mathcal{D}(e)} \left\{ t_{\text{tx}} \;\middle|\; t_{\text{valid}} \le t_{\text{cut}} \;\land\; t_{\text{tx}} \le t_{\text{cut}} \right\}$$ Prevents both valid-time lookahead and transaction-time backfill leakage in pre-seal NFL feature construction.
primitives.latex: $$F(e, t_{\text{cut}}) = \arg\max_{(v, t_{\text{valid}}, t_{\text{tx}}) \in \mathcal{D}(e)} \left\{ t_{\text{tx}} \;\middle|\; t_{\text{valid}} \le t_{\text{cut}} \;\land\; t_{\text{tx}} \le t_{\text{cut}} \right\}$$
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$F(e, t_{\\text{cut}})$:': 'Bi-temporal point-in-time value for entity e at cut time', '$\\mathcal{D}(e)$:': 'Dataset of all observed tuples for entity e', '$(v, t_{\\text{valid}}, t_{\\text{tx}})$:': 'Value v observed with valid-time t_valid and transaction-time t_tx', '$t_{\\text{cut}}$:': 'Reference time for the join operation (datetime)', '$\\arg\\max$:': 'Operator returning the tuple with maximum value'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Temporal data has explicit valid-time and transaction-time dimensions', 'No gaps exist in the observation timeline for any entity', 'Transaction times are monotonically increasing for a given entity', 'The dataset is finite and well-indexed for efficient range queries']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violating PIT joins allows future information to contaminate training sets, leading to overly optimistic model performance estimates that degrade in production due to lookahead bias.
